issue_context.title: Performance issue with DefaultStatsPrinterPlugin.js
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template because we'll close your issue -->
<!-- Before creating an issue please make sure you are using the latest version of webpack. -->

# Bug report

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the webpack Gitter. -->
<!-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=webpack -->
<!-- https://gitter.im/webpack/webpack -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

**What is the current behavior?**

DefaultStatsPrinterPlugin.js is slow to process/display results when large error message is returned.

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**

Reproduction in repo: https://github.com/martinsp/webpack-printer-issue running `npx webpack` will take significant amount of time

I have narrowed the issue down to this line: https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/14dd4f912c013f060bf7843a3d5462a51ff3051b/lib/stats/DefaultStatsPrinterPlugin.js#L1163 when it's commented out then the webpack command completes within a short amount of time

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub repository -->
<!-- The most helpful is a minimal reproduction with instructions on how to reproduce -->
<!-- Repositories with too many files or large `webpack.config.js` files are not suitable -->
<!-- Please only add small code snippets directly into this issue -->
<!-- https://gist.github.com is a good place for longer code snippets -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader, please create an issue on the loader/plugin repository instead -->

**What is the expected behavior?**

webpack results shown in a short amount of time

<!-- "It should work" is not a helpful explanation -->
<!-- Explain exactly how it should behave -->

**Other relevant information:**
webpack version:  5.62.1
Node.js version: v17.0.1
Operating System: macOS Monterey
Additional tools:
comments:
Unfortunatelly I don't see a lot of improvement after the fix. 

These are my findings after running `time yarn run webpack` with the code in https://github.com/martinsp/webpack-printer-issue

```
# current 5.62.1 release
webpack 5.62.1 compiled with 2 errors in 1314 ms
yarn run webpack  81.29s user 0.23s system 100% cpu 1:20.94 total

# with uncommented regex line
webpack 5.62.1 compiled with 2 errors in 1316 ms
yarn run webpack  2.42s user 0.13s system 127% cpu 2.005 total

# with "webpack": "webpack/webpack#12e028518a726c4ebf336ecfe823d27f51776b13" in package.json
webpack 5.62.1 compiled with 2 errors in 1332 ms
yarn run webpack  69.06s user 0.16s system 100% cpu 1:08.57 total
```

Maybe there is a way to return early from `formatError` in `DefaultStatsPrinterPlugin.js` when webpack is run with `--no-color` option?
You have very big error message, and regexp spend time to highlight error message, why do not avoid errors? It is non normal usage and the error should be fixed

I agree that this is somewhat an edge case, maybe mini-css-extract-plugin should limit the size of an error message.

I would gladly like to have a "write error-less code" superpower unfortunately I don't :(

The thing is that mini-css-extract-plugin is included in the default config of rails/webpacker project (upcoming v6) and if I include large css framework like Bootstrap and I have a typo/error in a css file, the compilation gets stuck for at least 1 minute. For my own usage I can fork the webpack project and return early from formatError and never worry about that again in my own projects. But I think quite a few users would be bitten by this behavior because ~~this can be triggered from default Rails 6 install~~ when rails/webpacker v6 will be released soon, the issue will be triggered by a lot more users.

I don't mind if you close the ticket. I know how to workaround the issue if I'll encourage it during refactoring in some of my projects.

Edit: clarified the Rails 6 vs upcoming rails/webpacker v6

Actually I'm not sure if the mini-css-extract-plugin is responsible for the large error message. I just observed that when 'style-loader' is used instead of mini-css-extract-plugin the error message is much shorter and does not include the generated code. I don't have enough knowledge of inner working of webpack to draw any conclusions
@martinsp yes this is on webpack side

review_comments: @vankop make sense to look at other `.+` places
Also small test to avoid regressions
